headline: Local DJ Forced To Transition Career After 'Bhajan Clubbing' Crowd Demands 4-Hour Extended Remix Of Hanuman Chalisa
body:
Nitin Khanna, a professional nightclub DJ who has spent the last decade perfecting the art of bass-heavy EDM, is currently retraining as a ‘spiritual beat-mixer’ after a recent boutique event in Delhi left him unable to play a single non-religious track for six hours. The shift came after organizers requested a 'high-tempo spiritual vibe,' which resulted in the crowd aggressively chanting for faster drops during traditional devotional hymns.

“I tried to slip in a standard techno beat, but the audience started doing rhythmic dandiya circles around the DJ booth while glaring at my laptop,” said Khanna, who has since spent his entire savings on an Ableton plugin pack that converts temple bells into heavy synth leads. “They didn't want house music. They wanted the drop to hit exactly when the incense sticks reached peak smoke density.”

Industry analysts note that this trend is rapidly turning local nightlife upside down, with popular clubs now replacing their strobe lights with dim clay lamps and substituting premium gin cocktails for unlimited servings of chilled buttermilk. For Khanna, the pivot is personal; he is currently practicing his 'shlokas' over drum-and-bass beats to ensure he remains booked for the upcoming wedding season, where he expects 'Om' loops to be the new industry standard for late-night dance floors.
